clue.text: Upset apple cart, ignoring European rubbish

indicators.note: an upset cart spills its load, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
ignoring something leaves it out, so one letter is dropped from the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over the apple cart and dismisses a European complaint as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring European' drops the E from APPLE CART, leaving APPLCART, which 'Upset' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are synonyms for nonsense or empty talk meant to impress.

clue.text: Turned up to get on with last part of mythical story

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning a word up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: to get on well with people is to gel with them
the end is the last part of anything

explanation.surface: Someone reaches the closing chapter of a myth after turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reverses GEL to LEG; 'to' and 'with' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional tale of heroes and wonders, told as if historical, is a mythical story.

clue.text: Bolt in trouble, turned up nursing broken toes at end of race

indicators.note: nursing means holding, so one piece wraps around the others
in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to dog someone is to trouble or plague them

indicators.note: broken signals the letters of the word toes are rearranged
at end of picks the final letter of the word race

explanation.surface: An athlete in trouble limps home at the end of the race with broken toes.
explanation.walkthrough: DOG 'turned up' gives GOD, which holds TOSE (the anagram of TOES, from 'broken') plus E. 'Bolt' looks like a sprinter, but it is the gardening sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that bolts shoots up and runs to flower and seed, ceasing to be useful, an idiom for decline.

clue.text: Round Table member finds cart carrying the heads of Guinevere and Arthur

indicators.note: the heads of the two names are their first letters

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm cart or wagon

explanation.surface: A knight is found with the heads of the queen and king in his wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gawain was one of King Arthur's knights, who sat at the Round Table.

clue.text: Pluck wings of excellent chicken

parts.note: to pluck at something is to pull it

indicators.note: a word's wings are its two outer letters

explanation.surface: A cook plucks the wings of a fine chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' and 'wings' look like kitchen work on the bird, but they are a verb meaning pull and the ends of 'excellent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hen, under a year old, is a specific kind of chicken.

clue.text: Beat Irishman to get short part in play

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is the stock Irishman of crosswords

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an actor's part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: An Irish actor beats out rivals to land a small part in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' is a noun here, a police officer's round.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer's beat is the regular round they walk or patrol.

clue.text: Enjoy eating silver plant

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to love something is to enjoy it
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys eating a silvery plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovage is an aromatic herb of the celery family, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Pass gargoyle's bottom left on part of church

indicators.note: in a down clue a word's bottom is its last letter

parts.note: the apse is the rounded end section of a church

explanation.surface: A gargoyle's lower half is left perched on the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that passes is said to go by, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Naughty Peter cheats to become classroom's blue-eyed boy

indicators.note: naughty behaviour is disorderly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naughty Peter cheats his way into favour in class.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that the boy who cheats becomes the favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-eyed boy is a favourite, and in a classroom that is the favoured pupil, an idiom.

clue.text: Priest tucking into old important part of diet

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so one letter sits within the other word

parts.note: stale food or ideas are old

explanation.surface: A priest tucks into stale food, the mainstay of his meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating, but it only places P inside STALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple food is a basic, main item eaten regularly, like rice or bread.

clue.text: Single about American with brightly coloured old bomber

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lone means single or solitary
gay in its older sense means bright and colourful

explanation.surface: A single person admires a brightly coloured vintage plane from America.
explanation.definitionFit: This B-29 aircraft dropped the atomic bomb on Hiroshima in 1945, a famous bomber of history.

clue.text: Rocket with special propeller?

parts.note: an oar propels a rowing boat

explanation.surface: A rocket fitted with a special propeller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocket' is a verb here, to rise fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that rocket rise steeply, a verb synonym for climbing high.

clue.text: Side with niece, furious about resistance to part of divorce proceedings

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the R
furious suggests wild disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone sides with a furious niece as she resists her divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furious' gives DECEENISI, and 'about' wraps that around R after the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the provisional court order in English law, made before the final decree absolute ends a marriage.

clue.text: Saw leader of Keystone Cops coming back for dessert

parts.note: to spot something is to see it, so spotted means saw

indicators.note: coming back means the letters are read in reverse
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the CID is the British Criminal Investigation Department, plain-clothes police

explanation.surface: Someone saw the head of the Keystone Cops return for pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' reverses K plus CID to give DICK. Keystone Cops were bumbling silent-film policemen. The answer is a British suet pudding with currants.
explanation.definitionFit: This steamed suet pudding studded with dried fruit is a traditional British dessert.

clue.text: Soldier briefly sheltering in shade of tree

indicators.note: a piece sheltering in another sits inside it

parts.note: a shade, as in a shade too much, is a tad, a small amount

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving at sea

explanation.surface: A soldier briefly takes cover in the shade of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' suggests shadow, but it means a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarind is a tropical tree bearing pods of tart pulp used in cooking.

clue.text: Put out to be taken in by damn pickpocket

indicators.note: being taken in by another word means sitting inside it

parts.note: to damn someone is to curse them

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so the letters of put are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone, put out, is fooled by a damned pickpocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PUT to UTP, which goes into CURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a thief who cut purses from belts, hence a pickpocket.

clue.text: Highlight small lock

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: A hairdresser adds a highlight to a small lock of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highlight' and 'lock' suggest hairdressing, but the first is a verb meaning emphasise.
explanation.definitionFit: To highlight a point is to emphasise it, a synonym for laying weight on it.

clue.text: Brave pull by youth leader

parts.note: to pluck at something is to pull it

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A youth leader gives a brave pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with pluck has courage, so the adjective means brave.

clue.text: Manual worker translated Mao sonnets

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A labourer has translated Chairman Mao's sonnets.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who cuts and lays stone works with his hands, a kind of manual worker.

clue.text: Secured lead in new organisation

indicators.note: giving letters a new organisation rearranges them

explanation.surface: A new organisation has secured the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead in' looks like part of the story, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fixed in place with metal pins has been secured, a synonym.

clue.text: Mate captured by crew coming back for incendiary fuel

indicators.note: being captured by a word means sitting inside it
in a down clue coming back means the word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
a pal is a mate or friend

explanation.surface: A shipmate captured by the crew comes back with firebomb fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' reverses MAN to NAM, which holds PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: This jellied petrol used in firebombs is a burning, incendiary fuel.

clue.text: Rabbit found in hospital kitchens

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A rabbit has been discovered in the hospital kitchens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is a British informal verb meaning to chatter on, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit on is to chatter at length, so it means speak or chat.

clue.text: Line edited in letter by politician cut short

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a Green is a member of an environmentalist party

explanation.surface: A line is edited in a letter by a politician cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of descent or ancestry is a family lineage, a synonym for breeding.

clue.text: Drink claiming Australian with large belly

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink served from a bowl

explanation.surface: Drinking has given an Australian a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-belly or protruding stomach is a large belly, a synonym.

clue.text: Colour of medicinal plant containing iodine

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the letter goes inside the plant's name

parts.note: senna is a plant used as a laxative
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A medicinal plant with added iodine gives off a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownish earth pigment and its yellow-brown or reddish-brown shade, so a colour.

clue.text: Loud insect drowning a request for silence

indicators.note: drowning puts something under, so the letters go inside the word

parts.note: a fly is an insect
sh is the sound made to ask for quiet

explanation.surface: A loud insect drowns out a request for silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud' means garish or showy, not noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud clothes are gaudy and showy, a synonym for ostentatious.
